attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps the antecedent (Microsoft unable to keep subsidizing) and the universal consequent. The hedged 'arguably' ranking is correctly treated as reasoning.

contract.note: Reading 'can't afford' as financial inability, not a pricing choice, is ordinary and is flagged. No subsidy size or test was supplied, so interpretation drives the result.

evidence.note: Microsoft FY26 Q4 release, available before the evaluation date. Shows large shareholder returns; does not show inability to fund compute subsidies.

reviews.rationale: Conditional claim whose antecedent is not established: no evidence shows Microsoft became financially unable to keep subsidizing compute. Per policy, a conditional with an unknown antecedent is not scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own statement; the 50% figure is his own assertion.

semantics.note: Present-tense concentration claim. 'Unclear' about other customers is hedged, and the nonpayment clause describes a vulnerability, not a forecast.

contract.note: Measuring by capacity share and using an April 2026 snapshot are ordinary readings given the GW context.

evidence.note: CoreWeave–Meta deal of April 9 shows a customer outside the two labs. It gives no construction-capacity share, so it does not settle the 50% figure.

reviews.rationale: No April inventory ties capacity under construction to its ultimate customers, so the 50% share can be neither confirmed nor refuted. The Meta evidence qualifies the hedged aside only.

semantics.note: Firm 'will take years' is a forecast with the 'even if OpenAI pays' best-case qualifier kept. 'Mortgaging its future' is rhetorical framing.

contract.note: Profit could mean periodic earnings or payback of upfront costs. The speaker's framing leans toward payback, but the contract flags this and requires reporting it separately. Acceptable.

evidence.note: Oracle Investor Day remarks dated the evaluation date, a company disclosure. They describe capital intensity but give no Stargate project profit timeline.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated, and there are no project-level accounts or payment records. The evidence cannot show when, or whether, Stargate projects first turn a profit.

semantics.note: 'Inevitable fall' is an unhedged prediction of an outcome with no date. 'Only delayed' adds a causal element.

contract.note: Reading 'fall' as a broad commercial collapse, not a stock dip or a single failure, is ordinary. No deadline is imported.

evidence.note: Anthropic S-1 announcement of Oct 26, a company disclosure. Shows ongoing capital-markets activity; it does not decide eventual collapse.
Kiplinger analyst piece dated the evaluation date. Calls it 'late cycle', not a confirmed peak; no collapse is established.

reviews.rationale: Undated forecast of eventual collapse. No industry-wide collapse is shown by the cutoff, and continuing operation cannot disprove an undated claim. The causal 'only delayed' part is untested.
